reasoning_traces.think:
Flow motifs are derived from temporal graph structures of possession-passing networks, where nodes represent players and directed edges denote passes within a 5-second window. Each motif represents a recurring subgraph pattern indicating specific tactical behaviors. The frequency of these motifs provides a statistical signature for individual and collective play styles. This enables GSI to perform Bayesian inference on player performance metrics by comparing observed motif distributions against prior expectations. Meanwhile, GSE leverages the motif space as a discrete state transition system, allowing it to predict next-best actions based on current possession states. The dual nature of motifs—both descriptive and prescriptive—enables robust modeling of agent behavior and strategic evolution. Failure modes arise when pass timing exceeds thresholds or game events interrupt sequences, invalidating motif integrity.
